title: How Stroppy Cloud works
lead: What a benchmark is built from, what happens on launch and where each part runs. Your data and machines stay in your cloud.

model.title: What you do and what you get

all.title: Overview
all.body: On the left is what you describe once and reuse across tests: databases and workloads. In the middle sit the test and the three ways to launch it, and on the right the report a run leaves behind. Hover a block for an example and details.

first.title: First run
first.body: Describe a database (say, PostgreSQL 17 on three nodes with Patroni) and a workload (TPC-C for 10 minutes), make a test from them, add your cloud key and press Launch. The stand comes up on its own, and the report appears once the load ends.

compare.title: Compare variants
compare.body: A suite is for questions like “which is faster”: PostgreSQL 16 or 17, S machines or M. You list the variants, the suite runs them all and puts the results in one table.

regress.title: Watch for regressions
regress.body: A schedule launches a test or a suite on cron, every night for example. If a new DBMS version or new settings turn out slower, you see it on the history chart before your users do.

share.title: Show the result
share.body: The report opens by a public link, no sign-in needed. You can send a run to the public rating, where it's ranked against setups of the same sizes, and embed that rating on your own site.

model.lead: You describe a database and a workload, pick machine sizes and launch the test. Stroppy Cloud then brings up machines in your cloud, installs the DBMS, drives the load and tears the stand down, and you keep a report you can compare with earlier runs or send to colleagues as a link.

arch.title: Stroppy Cloud architecture

console.title: Console
console.more: A single-page app. It reads data from the Stroppy Cloud server over REST and gets the live run (logs, metrics, progress) over one WebSocket, with no page reloads.
console.tech: in the browser · React · Grafana UI

api.title: Server
api.more: The product server; everything a user does goes through it: tenants and roles, the library, building a test into a full RunSpec, quotas, launching in Graphene, the live run, rating, compare and public reports.

identity.title: Accounts
identity.more: Sign up, sign in, e-mail confirmation and recovery by code. A session becomes a short-lived JWT; the server checks its signature itself, with no call per request.
identity.tech: JWT ES256 · checked on the server

state.title: Server database
state.more: Everything created in the console, plus the list and results of runs. Cloud keys aren't here: they're stored as secrets in the tenant's namespace in Graphene.

pipes.title: Pipelines
pipes.more: The run's code, in plain Go: create the network and machines, deploy containers, drive the load segments, collect the result. It ships in one image with the server, which publishes the binaries and manifests into every tenant's namespace on start.

door.title: Graphene server
door.more: Everyone reaches Graphene through one port: management (Connect), workers and agents (gRPC), the image registry (/v2), telemetry intake (OTLP). The server checks namespace access and drives the runs.

temporal.title: Temporal
temporal.more: In Temporal a run is a workflow, and each of its resources (a machine, a container, an artifact, the stand) is a separate record with an owner. That's why resources always get removed, children before their parent, and a crashed worker doesn't lose the run.

facts.label: Guarantees
items: a run survives a worker crash

worker.title: Run worker
worker.more: When a run starts, Graphene starts a container with the pipeline image. It drives the workflow through its phases and stops once the run is over and all its resources are gone.

crossplane.title: Run resources
crossplane.more: The part of the pipeline that declares the network, subnet, security group and VMs as resources of the run. Graphene owns them and removes them in order: machines first, then the network.

telemetry.title: Telemetry
telemetry.more: Everything a run writes about itself, over standard protocols. The Stroppy server reads it through Graphene with the tenant's rights, so the storage addresses stay inside.

agent.title: Agent
agent.more: Installed by cloud-init, it keeps its own outgoing gRPC session to Graphene (opens no ports), starts the run's containers and ships their telemetry.

db.title: Database
db.more: The chosen DBMS and topology (nodes, replicas, proxies) run as docker images on the stand machines for as long as the run goes, unless you keep the stand.

runner.title: Runner
runner.more: A separate machine with stroppy: loads the data and drives the scenario in segments; metrics leave through the agent.

all.title: Overview
all.body: Three zones: the Stroppy Cloud product (the console in your browser and the server), Graphene, which runs the pipelines, and your cloud with the stand. Each zone lists its dependencies underneath; hover a block to see what it depends on.

launch.title: Launch
launch.body: The console asks the server to launch a test. The server checks rights and quotas, builds the test into a RunSpec and starts the run in Graphene, which records it as a workflow in Temporal.

pipeline.title: Pipeline
pipeline.body: Graphene starts a worker with the stroppy-run image from its registry. The Stroppy server uploaded that image on start, so the pipeline's version always matches the server's.

stand.title: Stand
stand.body: The worker declares the network and machines; Crossplane creates them in your account with the tenant's key. An agent comes up on every machine and connects to Graphene by itself.

run.title: Run
run.body: Agents start the database, proxy and exporter containers; the stroppy runner loads data and drives the load segments through the proxy.

observe.title: Observe
observe.body: The agent scrapes the exporters and sends metrics and logs over OTLP to Graphene; artifacts go to S3. The server reads all of it through Graphene and pushes it to the console over WebSocket.

arch.lead: What runs in Stroppy Cloud, what runs in Graphene and what runs in your cloud, and how the parts talk while a benchmark is on.

network.title: Network
network.more: The first resource of a run in your cloud. Machines are created inside this network and removed with it.

proxy.title: Proxy and consensus
proxy.more: The cluster's entry point and its state store: etcd remembers Patroni's leader, HAProxy checks /primary and routes to the current leader. A single-node topology has neither.

exporters.title: Exporters
exporters.more: Machine and DBMS exporters run next to the database. The agent scrapes them and sends their metrics, together with stroppy's, to Graphene over OTLP.

blobs.title: Artifacts
blobs.more: Files the run takes from the machines: stroppy's raw output and the report. Kept in S3, they outlive the stand.

kratos.title: Ory Kratos
kratos.more: A separate self-hosted install: sign-up, sign-in, email verification, recovery by code and TOTP, with its own database in Postgres. The server doesn't call it per request; it only checks the JWT signature.

k8s.title: Kubernetes
k8s.more: The platform Graphene runs on. For each run it creates a worker Deployment with the pipeline image and deletes it when the run is over. Crossplane runs here too.

xp.title: Crossplane
xp.more: Creates networks and machines in your account through the tenant's ProviderConfig, built from its secret, and removes them in a cascade with the run.

oci.title: Docker registry
oci.more: Tenants' pipelines: a manifest and an image. Identical layers are stored once and served through Graphene (/v2); the registry itself isn't reachable from outside.

vm.title: Cloud
vm.more: Your account: the network and VMs are created in it with the tenant's key and removed after the run. You pay the cloud directly.

docker.title: Docker
docker.more: DBMS, proxies and exporters ship as docker images only; nothing gets installed on the host. The agent starts the run's containers and removes them when the run ends.

provisioning.title: Stand
provisioning.body: Stroppy Cloud creates the network and machines in your cloud with your key, and an agent starts on each machine.

deploying.title: Deploy
deploying.body: The agents start the DBMS in containers, the cluster forms, and the stand passes its checks before any load.

workload.title: Load
workload.body: stroppy drives the load segment by segment while you watch QPS, latency and logs in the console.

collecting.title: Collect
collecting.body: Metrics from the load window go into the report.

teardown.title: Teardown
teardown.body: The machines are removed unless you asked to keep the stand. The report stays.
